key_insight: The paper introduces “Pauli flat” states—N-qubit states with equal-magnitude Pauli expectations—that reproduce the correlation patterns of highly magical states without necessarily being magical themselves.
engineering_relevance: This gives a new route to model, detect, or benchmark quantum resources using Pauli correlation structure, with potential impact on error correction, state certification, and magic-sensitive estimation tasks.
method: Define Pauli flat states via uniform absolute values of all Pauli-string expectation values.
Compare these states to T-type and Hoggar states, including interpretations as mixed Pauli-covariant SIC/Weyl-Heisenberg-like fiducials.
Use a tailored magic witness plus analysis of entanglement and Bell nonlocality to classify examples inside and outside the stabilizer polytope.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit constructions and examples of these states, together with a magic witness and characterization of their entanglement/nonlocality properties.
watch_item: Equal Pauli magnitudes do not guarantee genuine magic, so practical use as a magic proxy may require extra witness checks to avoid false positives.
paper_title: Pauli Flat Quantum States Mimicking Maximal Magic
